summary: Affinity header truncation causes pinned-session stall and mirror-induced fallback during canary mirror
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightDoc reported repeated requests unexpectedly losing model pin affinity during a staged canary with mirror enabled; pinned sessions were stuck in a stalled state and traffic was routed to the canary mirror variant which later triggered a fallback to a degraded variant, producing mixed outputs and a billing spike.

Impact:
- Multiple BrightDoc tenants experienced mixed model outputs for ~90 minutes.
- Extra compute billed (mirror + fallback) estimated.
- Observed increase in user-facing latency for pinned sessions.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod-us-east)
- Customer tier: enterprise (BrightDoc Health)
- Affected model: redwood-alpha-v2 pinned by tenant route
- Canary configuration: mirror=true, canary_weight=5%, prewarm=true

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Create route with explicit pin to redwood-alpha-v2.
2) Enable canary mirror to new variant redwood-alpha-v2-canary.
3) Send burst of long-lived streaming sessions with custom X-Tenant-Affinity header containing tenant-specific token (>128 chars).
4) Observe that some sessions report pinned version in logs but requests are serviced by mirror then fallback.

Observed behavior:
- Edge logs show X-Tenant-Affinity header being truncated by the edge-proxy (header length limit).
- Orchestrator treats truncated affinity as a new session; mirror path commits a transient pin on the canary shard.
- When mirror health dipped, routing fallback logic rerouted those same requests to a degraded compatibility variant rather than original pinned model.
- Customer saw mixed outputs and a 2x token billing for affected sessions.

Expected behavior:
- Affinity header should be preserved end-to-end or trimmed deterministically such that orchestrator rehydrates existing pin.
- Mirror traffic should not be able to create a persistent pin for tenant sessions unless explicit promote is triggered.

Logs / telemetry pointers:
- Edge proxy traces: edge-proxy-traces/2026-03-10/brightdoc/trace-9987 (header length=128 -> truncated at 96)
- Router telemetry: router.events/tenant=brightdoc/pin-change/2026-03-10
- Serving runtime metrics: serving/runtime/pin-commits: spike coincident with mirror window 03:12-04:45 UTC

Initial hypothesis:
- Edge header normalization has a silent length-cut behavior for unknown headers, causing tenant affinity tokens to be altered.
- Mirror commit path currently accepts pin commitments from mirrored requests if the mirror shares identity metadata, creating a transient but sticky pin in the canary shard.

Immediate workaround given to customer:
- Disable canary mirror for the pinned route OR shorten tenant affinity tokens below the edge header truncation threshold.
- Temporary rate cap for long-lived streams applied on customer route to limit billing impact.

Requested outcome:
- Root-cause fix preventing mirror from committing tenant pins unless promote flag is explicit.
- Edge proxy change to preserve or consistently hash/namespace affinity headers.
- Postmortem and billing remediation for BrightDoc.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC - Triage: Confirmed customer telemetry and reproduced truncation with internal test harness using >120 char affinity token.
2026-03-10 07:20 UTC - Eng (Liang): Edge-proxy config shows default header size 96 bytes for unknown headers; not applied to standard cookie headers.
2026-03-10 08:05 UTC - Routing team: Mirror commit flow accepts pin-commit events without requiring 'promote' flag when request provenance==mirror; this was an optimization gone wrong.
2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - Reproduction: Created AB test with mirror=true, sent tokens of 140 chars; observed router pin table entries pointing at canary shard id 0x7f2b and TTL=7d (unexpected).
2026-03-11 02:10 UTC - Correlation: Billing spike correlates with duration mirror window when many long-lived sessions were affected (approx 1h30m).
comments: 2026-03-10 06:10 Sofia Patel (CS): Raised after BrightDoc reported mixed outputs. Attached sample request IDs and logs. Asked for urgent triage due to enterprise contract SLA.

2026-03-10 06:45 Liang Chen (Eng): Reproduced locally. Edge truncation reproduces with our internal long-token harness. Opening quick mitigation: disable header truncation for X-Tenant-Affinity on edge-proxy. (PR planned)

2026-03-10 07:05 Tomás Rivera (Routing): Found mirror commit path accepts pin commits from mirror traffic. Proposed change: require explicit 'pin_source'==controlplane OR require promote flag for mirror-origin commits.
2026-03-10 08:00 Sofia Patel (CS): Applied temporary mitigation on customer route (mirror disabled) and notified BrightDoc. Customer confirms mixed outputs stopped after mitigation.
2026-03-11 11:30 Aisha Kumar (SRE): Deployed hotfix to routing to reject pin commits from mirror-origin requests. Monitoring for regressions.
workaround: Disable canary mirror on the affected route OR shorten X-Tenant-Affinity tokens. Temporary rate cap applied to limit billing exposure.
root_cause: Two contributing faults: 1) Edge-proxy header normalization silently truncating non-standard long affinity header values, changing the identity token. 2) Mirror commit flow allowed mirror-origin requests to create persistent pin entries without an explicit promote signal.
resolution: Partial fix deployed: edge-proxy config adjusted to preserve X-Tenant-Affinity up to 256 bytes and routing service patched to ignore pin-commit events originating from mirror traffic unless promote flag present.
resolution_notes: Hotfixes: 1) edge-proxy: increased header limit + explicit whitelist for X-Tenant-Affinity. 2) router: added origin check and promote requirement for pin commits (PRs referenced). We plan a follow-up to add automated tests and a canary-blocklist for pin-commits from mirror paths.
follow_up_tasks: Add regression tests for header preservation across edge-proxy variants (owner: Edge)
Add unit/integration tests to prevent mirror-origin pin commits (owner: Routing)
Billing reconciliation: calculate overcharged tokens and issue credit to BrightDoc (owner: Finance/CS)
Postmortem and runbook update: explicitly document pin commit policy for mirror/traffic-mirroring workflows (owner: Platform)
public_communication: CS informed BrightDoc privately; will not post to status page. Postmortem will be shared with customer after internal review.
